literal: For sickness, medicine is other things indeed; she who wears beautiful ornaments, for her own affliction, she herself is the medicine.
translation: For ordinary diseases, the remedies lie in other external things; but for the affliction caused by this jewel-adorned maiden, she herself is the only cure.
modern: நோய்க்கு மருந்துகள் வேறு பொருள்களாக இருக்கின்றன; ஆனால், ஆபரணங்களை அணிந்த இவள் தந்த நோய்க்கு இவளே மருந்தாக இருக்கிறாள்.
explanation: In this couplet, the lover contrasts physical illnesses with the sweet affliction of love. For any common physical sickness, the cure is found in external medicines like herbs. However, for the pain of longing caused by this beautifully adorned maiden, no external remedy works. She who created the affliction is herself the only medicine that can heal him through her presence and union.
